nodes.text: Synthetic State K DOI Rule CLM-2026-04, effective 2026-04-01: for an accepted claim, payment must be issued no later than 15 calendar days after the insurer records a complete proof of loss.
Claim CLM-5521 status history records complete proof of loss at 2026-06-01T10:00:00Z and accepted coverage at 2026-06-02T09:00:00Z.
Payment workflow v3 starts its queue from notice_received_at and has no branch for complete_proof_of_loss_at. The procedure says payment is handled 'as soon as practical.'

Production PaymentJob schema contains notice_received_at and paid_at but no proof_of_loss_at, due_at, deadline_rule_id, alert, or escalation fields. The 2026-06 control inventory lists no external deadline service.
The June 2026 control test checked payment queue processing but did not calculate or alert on the 15-day interval from complete proof of loss.
Synthetic State M Claims Standard MS-18, version 2.1 effective 2026-05-15: an accepted payment is due within 10 business days after the completed proof-of-loss event, not after first notice.
Claim CLM-8802 has completed proof of loss at 2026-07-06T14:00:00Z. First notice was 2026-06-20; the claim was accepted on 2026-07-07.
Workflow v5 routes accepted claims to payment based on first_notice_at and a generic 30-day target. It has no business-day calculator for completed proof of loss and no breach escalation.
Production claim record stores first_notice_at and accepted_at, but completed_proof_at is free text in an adjuster note. Payment jobs have no rule ID, due date, calendar, or breach alert.
Compliance inventory for State M lists no scheduled control, report, or external service that calculates the 10-business-day deadline from completed proof of loss.
